elements.html:
Each of the 400 cases pairs a real customer question with a reference answer written by a support lead. The agent answers from what it retrieves, and a grader model checks every claim in the answer against the retrieved text.

  • Faithful: every claim is supported by a cited chunk
  • Correct: the answer matches the reference
  • Refused: the agent handed over to a person

Two reviewers re-grade a random 10 percent each week. They agree with the grader on 94 percent of cases, which is close to how often they agree with each other.

The suite runs on every prompt or retrieval change and blocks the merge if faithfulness drops by more than two points.
Up from 0.71 in June, on the same 400 cases

elements.content:
for case in suite:
    ctx = retrieve(case.q, k=8)
    out = agent(case.q, ctx)
    grade(out, case.ref, ctx)

report(suite, by="failure")

elements.html: Three changes that moved the score
Help articles are split at headings, around 300 tokens each. Answers stopped mixing steps from two products.
A cross-encoder reorders the top 50 search hits and keeps eight. Recall at eight rose from 0.81 to 0.93.
When no chunk scores above 0.4, the agent hands the ticket to a person instead of guessing.

slides.notes: Two columns: two 6x6 tiles, each a label, a 28px lead of up to two lines and 22px body. Suits before/after or problem/response.

elements.html: Fixed 1,000 token chunks, one search pass

Articles were cut every 1,000 tokens regardless of structure, so a chunk often held the end of one procedure and the start of another.

The agent quoted both. Graders marked 29 percent of answers unfaithful, and most of those cited a chunk that mentioned the right product in the wrong context.

A second search pass tried to fix recall and added 900 ms at p95.

Nobody could say which chunk an answer came from.

Articles are split at headings, so each chunk is one procedure or one policy. The title path is prepended to every chunk before embedding.

A cross-encoder rescores the top 50 hits in about 180 ms and keeps eight. The second search pass is gone.

Unfaithful answers fell to 13 percent and p95 latency to 2.1 seconds.

Every answer carries its chunk ids, so a failed case can be traced in the dashboard.

elements.html:
Search compares embeddings, which is fast and loose: the right article is usually in the top 50, rarely at the top. The cross-encoder reads the question and each chunk together and scores how well the chunk answers it.

Scoring 50 chunks takes about 180 ms on one L4 GPU. It replaced a second search pass that cost 900 ms and found less.

The model is a small cross-encoder fine-tuned on 12,000 question and chunk pairs graded by the support team, so it learns our products' names and the difference between plans.

The top score also drives refusal: under 0.4, the agent hands the ticket to a person.
